description: Load a category tree in one call — a whole department structure, a migration. For one or two categories use create_category. Parents and children may sit in the SAME batch: `parentRef` takes a parent NAME (matched inside this batch first, then against existing categories) or an existing id, which is what makes a flat spreadsheet importable. Loops and unresolvable parents fail those rows and their descendants, not the batch. This tool does NOT match rows against what already exists — the cabinet does that in the browser, not on the server. Every row in `creates` becomes a NEW record even if an identical one is already there. To change existing records, read them with export_records and pass their ids in `updates`. Two rows named the same thing in one batch, or a name that already exists, will produce two categories with that name. On `updates` this is the only import with true merge-patch semantics: omit a field to leave it, pass null to CLEAR it, and pass `parentId: null` to move a category back to the top level (which create_category and update_category cannot do). Products are untouched — importing categories neither assigns nor removes products; that is the products side. Rows are independent and per-row failures come back in the reply. Max 500 rows per call. BEFORE CALLING: show the merchant a preview of the first few rows, state the EXACT number of rows and which resource they hit, and get an explicit yes. There is NO undo and no dry-run — nothing here validates without writing. If you are unsure a row is right, ask; a wrong bulk import is far more expensive to repair than a question. Afterwards, tell the merchant what landed: an import done here does NOT appear in the cabinet's Recent Imports list, which only records uploads made through the wizard.

parentRef.description: Parent category NAME (this batch or existing) or an existing category id. Omit for top level

category.description: Only the fields to change; null clears

parentId.description: Category id — an id here, never a name. null makes it a top-level category

categoryId.description: Existing category id from export_records or get_categories
